claims.content: To allow the user to compress one or more files or archives into a single compressed archive file using PeaZip.

goal.raw_text: To allow the user to compress one or more files or archives into a single compressed archive file using PeaZip.

claims.content: The user has launched the PeaZip application and is viewing the file manager interface.
One or more files or folders intended for compression are visible and accessible within the current directory view in the file manager interface.
The user presses the 'Add' button on the toolbar in the file manager interface.

trigger.raw_text: The user presses the 'Add' button on the toolbar in the file manager interface.

claims.content: The user selects one or more files or folders to be compressed from the file manager interface.
The system opens the 'Create archive' window (also referred to as the Create archive Interface).
The user specifies the output path and filename for the new compressed archive.
The user selects the desired compression format (e.g., ZIP, 7Z) and adjusts optional settings such as compression level, splitting volumes, or encryption if required.
The user confirms the operation by clicking the 'OK' button in the 'Create archive' window.
The system compresses the selected objects into the specified archive format and saves the resulting file to the designated location.
Upon successful completion, the system displays a progress/completion dialog (PeaLauncher) and updates the file manager interface to reflect the newly created archive.
A new compressed archive file is created and saved at the user-specified location with the chosen name and format.
The original files or folders selected for compression remain unchanged in their original locations unless explicitly moved or deleted by the user.
If encryption was applied, the archive is secured with the specified password and/or keyfile.
The PeaLauncher window displays a 'Job successfully completed' status along with input/output size and processing time.
The file manager interface refreshes to show the newly created archive file in the current directory view.
